beats.say: Scientists use scientific notation to make long numbers easier to read without miscounting.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Each gold interval is one meter. Our survey continues beyond the ruler.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Watch ten one-meter intervals gather into one ten-meter interval. The length stays the same.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Another tenfold step gives hundred-meter intervals.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Then a thousand.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Ten thousand.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: A hundred thousand.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: And a million. Now the whole length fits.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Four point six counts the intervals; ten to the sixth tells how big each interval is.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Four point six is the coefficient. The raised six is the exponent, counting six tenfold steps from one.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: To recover ordinary digits, called standard form, multiply the coefficient by ten six times.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Each multiplication moves every digit into a larger place: first tens, then hundreds.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Then thousands, ten-thousands, and hundred-thousands.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: A common slip counts five zeros, but the leading four moves six places from ones to millions.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Reading backward, choose four point six. Six multiplications restore the original value.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: This specimen is zero point zero zero zero two five meters wide: too small for this scale.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Keep its width unchanged. Open one meter into tenths.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Then open a tenth into hundredths.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Open a hundredth into thousandths.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: And a thousandth into ten-thousandths. Now we can measure it.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Two point five intervals, each one ten-thousandth of a meter. Negative four means four divisions by ten; the length is positive.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Start with two point five and divide by ten.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The two moves into tenths, then hundredths.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Then thousandths, and finally ten-thousandths.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Reading backward, choose two point five. Four divisions recover the original value.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Four million six hundred thousand is four point six times ten to the sixth.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.label: Digits times a power of ten

beats.say: Zero point zero zero zero two five is two point five times ten to negative four.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Both write a positive number *N* as *a* times ten to *n*. Keep *a* at least one and below ten, so everyone writes the same number the same way.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The exponent *n* counts whole steps: positive goes up, negative goes down, and zero leaves the scale alone.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Keep one nonzero digit before the point. The exponent counts tenfold steps from the coefficient to the number.
beats.speaker: teacher
